title: Personal Checking: bank-error refund of an overdraft item fee
content:
## Situation and business effect

This entry applies to a Personal Checking account that carries an overdraft item fee, the fee charged when the bank pays a debit into overdraft. It governs whether that fee was charged in error and so whether the fee is returned to the owner as a bank-error correction. Where a refund is owed, the agent posts it, and the owner sees it in the account activity at once with the posted ledger balance raised by the refunded amount. Where no refund is owed, this entry posts nothing.

## Posting tool

Refunds under this entry use **refund_uncovered_overdraft_fee_6b0f4e50**. The agent first unlocks this internal tool (unlock_agent_discoverable_tool) and then calls it (call_agent_discoverable_tool).

**Effect of one call.** One call writes one refund entry on the account, dated today, that refunds the named overdraft item fee entry, records the refund as a bank-error correction for the overdraft item fee, and raises the account's posted ledger balance by the refunded amount at once. The tool records exactly the amount given against the named fee and does not check the fee, its date, its amount or any earlier refund.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Class | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| checking_account_id | Id | Reference number of the checking account that was charged the overdraft item fee (checking account lookup) | Reference number |
| customer_id | Id | Customer reference number of that account's owner (customer profile lookup) | Reference number |
| source_item_id | Id | Reference number of the overdraft item fee entry to be refunded (checking activity lookup) | Reference number |
| amount | Fixed format | The refund, in U.S. dollars and always positive | Plain number to 2 decimals, half-up, such as 12.34 |
| statement_cycle | Fixed format | Statement cycle of today's posting | YYYY-MM, naming the month in which the cycle closes |

## Return

On success the tool returns a confirmation sentence that names the new refund entry reference number, the fee entry it refunds, the amount refunded in USD with 2 decimal places, and the account's new posted ledger balance in USD with 2 decimal places. Receiving it means the refund is posted.

## Calling contract Q&A

**Q: Should source_item_id name the overdrawn debit or the fee?**
A: The overdraft item fee entry being refunded.

**Q: Does the tool confirm that the fee was charged in error?**
A: No. It does not check the fee, its date, its amount or any earlier refund; the decision is made before the call.

**Hypothetical call (illustrative references only):** checking_account_id "CHK-EXAMPLE", customer_id "CUST-EXAMPLE", source_item_id "ODF-EXAMPLE", amount 27.50, statement_cycle "2026-05". The receipt names the new refund entry, fee ODF-EXAMPLE, 27.50 USD refunded and the new ledger balance.
